newsitem.title: USA: Chevron Q4 chemical business earnings down.
newsitem.headline: Chevron Q4 chemical business earnings down.

text.p: - Chevron Corp achieved higher net earnings in the fourth quarter despite disappointing results in chemicals and downstream operations, the company said on Thursday.

Although higher oil and gas prices boosted upstream earnings, they severely squeezed margins for refined products such as gasoline and chemicals, the company said. Chevron Chairman Ken Derr said downstream and chemicals results suffered because market competition prevented the company from recovering higher raw material and fuel costs in the marketplace.

"Cost consciousness has become an essential part of the way we do business," Derr continued. "Although total operating and administrative expenses increased slightly in 1996, largely because of higher fuel and transportation costs, our per barrel expenses stayed about flat at $6.10."
Chevron attributed a significant improvement in U.S. upstream earnings for the year and fourth quarter to higher crude oil and natural gas prices.
For the year 1996, the company's average crude oil realization of $18.80 per barrel was $3.46 higher than the $15.34 averaged for 1995.
In the fourth quarter, average realizations were $21.32, up $6.38 per barrel from the prior-year quarter.
Strong international upstream results also reflected higher crude oil sales volumes and prices.

Although much improved from 1995, U.S. downstream results were depressed in 1996 by competitive conditions in many of the company's markets that did not allow the full recovery of higher crude oil costs and, in California, the increased manufacturing cost of the mandated cleaner-burning gasolines, Chevron said.
Product sales volumes in 1996 and 1995 averaged 1.12 million barrels per day. Fourth quarter sales volumes increased to 1.13 million barrels per day from 1.09 million in 1995.

Chevron's international refining and marketing results in 1996 were also depressed due to the inability to recover higher crude oil costs in the price of refined products, particularly in the company's Caltex affiliate's operating areas.
